dataset.name: Riverbank temperatures on the Selawik River, Alaska 2010-2012, and Koyukuk River, Alaska June to July 2018.
description: The data package includes temperature measurements from riverbanks along the Selawik and Koyukuk Rivers in northwest Alaska. The Selawik River data also includes meteorological data collected locally and the Koyukuk River includes bulk density and ice content data from the riverbanks. The Selawik River data was collected between 2010 and 2013 with meteorological data collected for the entire time period and riverbank temperatures collected in shorter time intervals between 2010 to 2012. All of the Selawik River data were collected a single river bend. The Koyukuk River temperature data was collected from late June to early July 2018 at a total of five locations on three riverbanks. Ice content measurements on the Koyukuk were made at five riverbank locations. The data collection on both rivers was done in support of studies on the influence of permafrost on riverbank erosion. The temperature data was collected to monitor the thermal conditions of the river banks both seasonally and during periods of erosion. The ice content of the banks was measured to better understand how bank erosion rates are influenced by ice in the frozen riverbanks.

measurementTechnique:
Selawik River Meteorological Data
Selawik River Meteorological Data (‘SelawikWxStn.csv’). Meteorological data measured on the Selawik River, Alaska. From October 2010 to July 2013 air temperature, relative humidity, radiation, shallow soil temerture and moisture, and wet precipitation measurements were made at 66.5006 N, 157.60967 W. The measurements were collected in a tussock tundra meadow just upslope from a retrogressive thaw slump. Data was recorded on a Campbell Scientific Inc. CR1000 datalogger. Air temperature and relative humidity were measured with a Campbell Scientific HMP50 Temperature & Relative Humidity Sensor. Accuracy of the temperature measurements from the HMP50 vary with temperature and range from plus or minus 1.2 degrees Celsius at the minimum values recorded to plus or minus 0.4 degrees Celsius over most temperature measurements recorded. The relative humidity measurements have a manufacturer reported accuracy of plus or minus 3 percent. Near ground surface and soil temperature measurements were made with a T109 sensor with and accuracy of 0.25 C. Both short and longwave radiation were measured with Campbell Scientific CNR2 Net Radiometer. Wet precipitation was measured with Campbell Scientific TE525 Tipping Bucket Rain Gage. Volumetric soil moisture was measured with a Campbell Scientific CS616 water content reflectometer. Soil moisture values were not adjusted to the site specific soil properties and represent the factor calibrated values with an accuracy of plus or minus 2.5 percent.

Selawik River riverbank temperatures:
Ground temperature measurements were measured at a bend of the Selawik River (66.48 N, 157.71 W) using a combination of Onset Computer Corporation Hobo Pendant (UA-001-08) Temperature sensors, Hobo U23-003 Temperature Sensor, and Campbell Scientific T109 temperature sensors. The Hobo Pendant sensor have a resolution of 0.14 degrees C and an accuracy of plus or minus 0.53 degree C. The Hobo U23 sensors have a resolution of 0.02 degrees C and an accuracy of plus or minus 0.21 degrees C. Soil moisture was also measured a two locations using the Campbell Scientific CS616 water content reflectometer.
‘unfrozenbank_2m_2010.csv’ – Ground temperature data recorded at the downstream end of the monitored bend in unfrozen deposits of sandy gravel. Two sets of Hobo U23-003 temperature sensors were installed at depths of 20, 40, 80, and 120 cm below the ground surface at a location (66.48181667 N, 157.7111667 W) 2 m from the edge riverbank on July 18, 2010. The sensors were downloaded on October 8, 2010, and subsequently lost due to bank erosion in early 2011.

Koyukuk River riverbank temperature data
Koyukuk River riverbank temperatures: Bank temperatures were measured at five locations along three riverbanks using an array of iButton loggers installed in a custom rod manufactured by Alpha Mach Inc. The sensor rods were inserted holes drilled horizontally into the frozen bank face. Aluminum shields were installed over the sensor rods to shade the bank and limit direct solar radiation on the bank face and temperature sensors. The temperature loggers were located 5cm in front of the bank face to measure the ambient air temperature, at the bank face (0 cm) and at intervals of 5, 10, 20, and 40 cm into the bank. The iButtons had a manufacturer reported resolution of 0.0625 degrees Celsius and an accuracy of plus or minus 0.5 degrees Celsius. Ice content of the bank materials the sensors were installed in are provided in KoyukukBankIceContent.csv.
‘KoyukukBank3b_153cm.csv’. Installed on the west bank of the Koyukuk River upstream of the Village of Huslia at 65.75232 N, 156.50511. The sensor rod was installed in fine sand, 153cm below the top of the riverbank. The sensor rods collected data from June 30 to July 3, 2018, at one minute intervals.

Koyukuk River riverbank ice content
Ice content of the riverbank materials was measured by collecting 210 ml volume samples of frozen bank material using a concrete corer attached to a power hammer drill. The samples were weighed and thawed, dried in a laboratory and the dry sample weight was recorded to determine the mass of water in the sample. The water mass was converted to ice volume and the total volumetric fraction of the ice in the sample was calculated. The sample at bank 1 was collected at a depth of 105 to 111 cm from core extracted from the top of the bank using a SIPRE corer.
